what: The class of every tool in Qonto's tool list, as the class and category rule on the Card must give it. A test of that rule: for each tool, the rule's class must equal this one, never lower.

classes.read: Reads only. Runs within the Card's scope.
classes.write: Changes something at the vendor that can be edited or undone. Held for the owner when the app's writes aren't proved.
classes.irreversible: Can't be undone once it runs: finalise (locks or numbers a document), send (reaches a third party), share (gives a person access). Refused until the owner opens it on the Card.
classes.money: Moves money, asks for it to move, decides on such a request, or issues or changes a payment instrument. Refused until the owner opens it on the Card, and each payment is still approved on the phone.
classes.delete: Removes something. Refused until the owner opens it on the Card.

rule: A tool is a read only when its readOnlyHint is true and its name starts with a read verb (get_, list_). Any disagreement, or a missing hint, makes it at least a write.
destructiveHint true makes it at least irreversible, unless its name is a delete (delete_, remove_), which makes it delete.
A tool is classed by the worst thing its arguments can do. An argument condition can lower the class only when the signed call fixes that argument's value.
A name that says send, finalise, mark paid or invite is irreversible whatever its hints say; a name about transfers, cards, payment links or money requests is money.
A tool not in this list gets its class from these rules and is never a read by default. A tool the vendor adds is never approved automatically.

send_invoices.what: The flagship's category: an approved invoice is finalised and sent. Each call is approved by fingerprint.
send_invoices.precondition: Before by_einvoice, the taf reads get_client and checks e_invoicing_reachable.

to_check: Qonto's live list stored on 28 Nov has 61 tools; this file lists every name in planque's reference plus create_transfer_request. Names here that the live list lacks are kept: if Qonto serves them later, their class is already set.

tools.name: create_client
tools.why: Creates a client record at Qonto; nothing leaves Qonto and it can be edited or deleted.

tools.name: update_client
tools.why: Edits a client record.

tools.name: create_quote
tools.why: Creates a quote at Qonto; sending it is send_quote.

tools.name: update_quote
tools.why: Edits a quote.

tools.name: create_product
tools.why: Creates a product in the catalogue.

tools.name: create_team
tools.why: Changes the organisation's teams.

tools.name: update_client_invoice
tools.why: Edits an invoice; Qonto allows it on drafts only.

tools.name: upload_attachment
tools.why: Attaches a file to a transaction.

tools.name: request_attachment_upload
tools.why: Opens an upload for an attachment.

tools.name: create_cash_flow_category
tools.why: Creates a cash-flow category.

tools.name: modify_transaction_cash_flow_category
tools.why: Recategorises a transaction.

tools.name: export_transactions
tools.why: 'export' isn't a read verb, so it isn't a read by name. An export can be delivered somewhere, so it's a write until its definition shows otherwise.

tools.name: export_transaction_attachments
tools.why: Same as export_transactions.

tools.name: create_client_invoice
tools.why: Classed by the worst thing its arguments can do: status unpaid finalises (numbered, locked). It's a write only when the signed call fixes status to draft.

tools.name: change_client_invoice_status
tools.why: finalize locks and numbers the invoice; cancel and unmark_as_paid change a final invoice. destructiveHint true.

tools.name: change_supplier_invoice_status
tools.why: Changes a supplier invoice's status. destructiveHint true.

tools.name: mark_client_invoice_as_paid
tools.why: destructiveHint is false, but it records a payment on a final invoice, and the consent page promises it is refused. The name decides when the hint says less.

tools.name: create_credit_note
tools.why: A credit note is a numbered accounting document issued against a final invoice. Classed as finalise until its definition shows a draft state.

tools.name: send_client_invoice
tools.why: Sends to a third party. by_einvoice submits to the e-invoicing network and can't be recalled; by email it reaches the client. destructiveHint true.

tools.name: send_quote
tools.why: Emails a third party. destructiveHint is false, but the name says send, so it's send, not write.

tools.name: create_reminder
tools.why: A reminder emails the client on a schedule; classed by what it does, not by its create name.

tools.name: create_membership
tools.why: Invites a person into the organisation and gives them access; access given can be used before it's removed.

tools.name: create_transfer_request
tools.why: Asks for money to move.

tools.name: create_multi_transfer_request
tools.why: Asks for several transfers.

tools.name: approve_request
tools.why: Approves a money request (Qonto answers with a deeplink to finish).

tools.name: decline_request
tools.why: Decides a money request. destructiveHint true. It's in the money category because it decides money, even though it moves none.

tools.name: create_card
tools.why: Issues a payment card.

tools.name: update_card
tools.why: Changes a card's limits or settings.

tools.name: change_card_status
tools.why: Locks, unlocks or ends a card. destructiveHint true.

tools.name: create_card_request
tools.why: Asks for a card.

tools.name: create_payment_link
tools.why: Creates a link a payer uses to pay; a payment instrument given to a third party.

tools.name: delete_client_invoice
tools.why: Deletes a draft invoice. destructiveHint true.

tools.name: delete_client
tools.why: Deletes a client record.

tools.name: delete_quote
tools.why: Deletes a quote.

tools.name: delete_reminder
tools.why: Deletes a reminder.

tools.name: remove_transaction_attachment
tools.why: Removes a transaction's attachment. destructiveHint true.
